classification.difficultyReason: Combines triangle properties, exterior angles, vertically opposite angles and a reflex angle.

inlines.text: Determine the value of the pronumeral, using all the angle relationships you know.
You do not need to show reasoning.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5a, lower grid, first row left
spec.description: Equilateral triangle ABC with BC extended to D and AC extended to E; a° lies between CD and CE.
spec.mathematics: All three sides have matching single ticks. Angle DCE is vertically opposite angle ACB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the unknown a° is visible in the question diagram.

answer.worked: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $a=60^{\circ}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5b, lower grid, first row centre
spec.description: Triangle ABC with A upper right, B below and C left. Interior angles at A and B are 22° and 29°. The unknown at C is explicitly marked by an exterior reflex arc.
spec.mathematics: The reflex angle at C is 360° minus the interior angle ACB.
spec.answerVisibility: 22°, 29° and a° are visible; the reflex-angle answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
Triangle angle sum:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB&=180^{\circ}-22^{\circ}-29^{\circ}\\\angle ACB&=129^{\circ}\end{aligned}$$
Angles around a point:
$$\begin{aligned}a&=360^{\circ}-129^{\circ}\\a&=231^{\circ}\end{aligned}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5c, lower grid, first row right
spec.description: Isosceles triangle ABC with AB=AC, angle ABC=72°, D on BC and AD perpendicular to BC. The unknown a° is angle DAC.
spec.mathematics: Equal base angles give angle ACB=72°. Right triangle ADC then gives angle DAC=18°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 72°, the right-angle square, matching double ticks and a° are visible.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5d, lower grid, second row left
spec.description: Triangle ABC with AC extended beyond both A and C. Exterior angles at A and C are 155° and 116°, respectively. The interior angle at B is a°.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAC=25° by supplementary angles. At C the exterior-angle theorem gives a+25°=116°.
spec.answerVisibility: 155°, 116° and a° are visible; no computed interior angles are supplied.

answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=180^{\circ}-155^{\circ}=25^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line).
Using the exterior angle theorem at $C$,
$$\begin{aligned}a+25^{\circ}&=116^{\circ}\\a&=91^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5e, lower grid, second row centre
spec.description: Isosceles triangle ABC with AC=BC. BC extends to D and AC extends to E. Angle DCE is 49° and the interior angle at B is a°.
spec.mathematics: Angle ACB is vertically opposite the 49° angle. The remaining two equal base angles each equal 65.5°.
spec.answerVisibility: 49°, matching double ticks and a° are visible; no computed angles are supplied.

answer.worked:
$\angle ACB=49^{\circ}$ (vertically opposite angles). Since $AC=BC$, the base angles are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}a&=\frac{180^{\circ}-49^{\circ}}{2}\\a&=65.5^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5f, lower grid, second row right
spec.description: Right triangle ABC with a right-angle square at A, BC extended through C to D, exterior angle ACD=150°, and interior angle ABC=a°.
spec.answerVisibility: The right-angle square, 150° and a° are visible; the answer is omitted.
